topic: Everest is not the closest point to space
claim: Earth bulges at the equator from its spin, so Ecuador's Chimborazo summit is over 2,072 m farther from Earth's center than Everest's, though Everest is higher above sea level (8,848 m vs 6,268 m).

beats.caption: Everest isn't closest to space
beats.vo: Everest isn't the closest point to space.

beats.caption: Highest above sea level: 8,848 m
beats.vo: Sure, it's the highest mountain above sea level, at 8,848 meters.

beats.caption: Earth's spin makes it bulge
beats.vo: But Earth isn't a perfect ball. Its spin makes it bulge around the equator.

beats.caption: Ecuador, on the equator
beats.vo: Ecuador's Chimborazo sits one degree south of the equator, right on that bulge.

beats.caption: 6,268 m up, 2,072 m farther out
beats.vo: Its summit is only 6,268 meters above sea level, yet over 2,000 meters farther from Earth's center than Everest's peak.

beats.caption: Farthest from Earth's center
beats.vo: NOAA confirms it: Chimborazo's peak is the farthest point on Earth from the planet's center.

beats.caption: Highest vs. farthest: which counts?
beats.vo: So Everest is highest above sea level, but Chimborazo's peak is closest to the stars. Which one should count?

sources.text: NOAA National Ocean Service, What is the highest point on Earth as measured from Earth's center? https://oceanservice.noaa.gov/facts/highestpoint.html
